Ukraine has also asked the UN agency to prohibit member countries from using Russian airspace, according to a government letter to the ICAO cited by Reuters. It came after Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned airlines to stay away. "We in Ukraine do not want innocent lives to be lost. That is why we are warning our partners: the safe days in Russia's skies are over," Zelenskyy said. "Drone-infested skies are no place for civilian aviation," he added. "The sky over Russia is currently for drones ... as long as the war continues." Last week, Zelenskyy threatened to deploy up to 1,000 long-range drones per day. The ICAO has not commented on the request from Ukraine. Russia 's aviation watchdog regularly closes airports in response to the Ukrainian drones. Ukraine's airspace has been closed since the war started in 2022. While European ​and US carriers do not fly over Russia due to the conflict, the airspace is used by other airlines from China, Turkey, the United Arab Emirates and other Gulf countries. https://www.baltictimes.com/latvijas_pas.text: Estonia Latvia Lithuania Business Analysis Opinions Culture EU Affairs Search Archive Latvijas Pasts to issue postage stamp dedicated to 250th anniversary of U.S. independence 2026-09-10 LETA/TBT Staff RIGA - On Friday, September 11, Latvia's national postal company Latvijas Pasts, in cooperation with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, will issue a stamp dedicated to the 250th anniversary of U.S. independence, LETA was told at the company. The new postage stamp will have a face value of EUR 4.41. The stamp will have a print run of 7,000 copies, and 500 specially designed envelopes will also be issued alongside the stamp. The philatelic issue was designed by artist Girts Griva. The unveiling of the philatelic issue will take place on September 11 at 9 a.m. at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, with Foreign Minister Baiba Braze (New Unity), U.S. Ambassador to Latvia Melissa Argyros, U.S. Ambassador to the European Union Andrew Puzder, and Latvijas Pasts board member Andris Purins scheduled to attend the event. Later, the special tribute will be delivered to the U.S. President. First-day postmarking will take place on Friday, September 11, from 9 a.m. to 6 p.m. at the Latvijas Pasts customer service center Elizabete. As reported, Latvijas Pasts had a turnover of EUR 82.706 million last year, which is 11.8 percent less than in 2024, but the company posted a profit of EUR 2.995 million in contrast to a loss the previous year. Latvijas Pasts provides postal services throughout the territory of Latvia. The company provides domestic and international deliveries, ranging from e-commerce and parcel deliveries to press, letter correspondence and personalized logistics solutions.
